A water drop of diameter \(2 \mathrm{~cm}\) is broken into 64 equal droplets. The surface tension of water is \(0.075 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}\). In this process the gain in surface energy will be:

 

[JEE Main 2022, 28 June (Shift 1)]

(a) Radius of drop, \(r=\frac{2}{2} \mathrm{~cm}=1 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}\)

Let the radius of droplet be \(r_{o}\)

Volume of drop \(=64 \times\) volume of droplet

\(\frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3}=64 \times \frac{4}{3} \pi r_{o}^{3}\)

\(r=4 r\)

\(r_{0}=\frac{1}{4} r\)

Initial surface area, \(A_{1}=4 \pi r^{2}\)

Gain in surface energy, \(\Delta U=T \Delta A\)

\(=2.8 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~J}\)

questions.question:
Let \(f: R \rightarrow R\) be defined as
\(
f(x)=\left[\begin{array}{cc}
{\left[e^x\right],} & x<0 \\
a e^x+[x-1], & 0 \leq x<1 \\
b+[\sin (\pi x)], & 1 \leq x<2 \\
{\left[e^{-x}\right]-c,} & x \geq 2
\end{array}\right.
\)
where \(a, b, c \in R\) and \([t]\) denotes greatest integer less than or equal to \(t\). Then, which of the following statements is true?

 

[JEE Main 2022, 28 Jun (Shift 1)]
options: There exists \(a, b, c \in R\) such that \(f\) is continuous on \(R\).
If \(f\) is discontinuous at exactly one point, then \(a+b\) \(+c=1\).
If \(f\) is discontinuous at exactly one point, then \(a+b\) \(+c \neq 1\)
\(f\) is discontinuous at atleast two points, for any values of \(a, b\) and \(c\)
questions.explanation:
For \(x<0\), we have \(0<e^x<1\),

so \([e^x]=0\)

For \(0\leq x<1\),

\(-1\leq x-1<0\),

so \([x-1]=-1\) and \(f(x)=ae^x-1\)

For \(1<x<2\),

\(\sin(\pi x)<0\),

so \([\sin(\pi x)]=-1\),

whereas at \(x=1\), \([\sin\pi]=0\)

Thus \(f(1)=b\), but the right-hand limit at \(x=1\) is \(b-1\).

Therefore, \(f\) is discontinuous at \(x=1\) for every choice of \(a,b,c\).

At \(x=0\), the left-hand limit is \(0\), while \(f(0)=a-1\)

Continuity at \(x=0\) requires \(a-1=0\),

so, \(a=1\)

For \(x\geq2\), \(0<e^{-x}<1\),

so \([e^{-x}]=0\) and \(f(x)=-c\)

The left-hand limit at \(x=2\) is \(b-1\).

Continuity at \(x=2\) requires \(b-1=-c\),

so, \(c=1-b\).

Hence \(f\) is discontinuous at exactly one point only when \(a=1\) and \(c=1-b\).

Then, \(a+b+c=1+b+1-b=2\ne1\)

If \(S_2\) is false, \(S_1\) is false, so option \(\mathrm{B}\) is true.

The claim that \(S_2\) is false while \(S_1\) is true is impossible, so option \(\mathrm{C}\) is not true.

If \(S_1\) is false, \(S_2\) is false, so option \(\mathrm{D}\) is true.

The correct option is \(\mathrm{C}\).

Let \(t=e^x\)

Since \(e^x>0\)

we have \(t>0\)

The equation becomes

\(t^4+4t^3-58t^2+4t+1=0\)

Since the coefficients are symmetric, divide by \(t^2\):

\(t^2+\frac{1}{t^2}+4\left(t+\frac{1}{t}\right)-58=0\)

\(y=t+\frac{1}{t}\)

\(t>0\)

Multiplying by \(t\)

\(t=3\pm2\sqrt2\)

Both values are positive

Since \(t=e^x\)

each positive value of \(t\) gives one real value of \(x\)

Therefore the number of real solutions is \(2\).

questions.question:
A ray of light passing through the point \( P(2,3) \) reflects on the \( x \)-axis at point \( A \) and the reflected ray passes through the point \( Q(5,4) \). Let \( R \) be the point that divides the line segment \( A Q \) internally into the ratio \( 2: 1 \). Let the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular \( M \) from \( R \) on the bisector of the angle \( P A Q \) be \( (\alpha, \beta) \). Then, the value of \( 7 \alpha+3 \beta \) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2022, 28 June (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Reflect the point \(P(2,3)\) in the \(x\)-axis to obtain \(P'(2,-3)\).

By the law of reflection, the broken path \(P\to A\to Q\) becomes the straight path \(P'\to A\to Q\).

Therefore, the reflection point \(A\) is the intersection of the line \(P'Q\) with the \(x\)-axis.

The slope of the line through \(P'(2,-3)\) and \(Q(5,4)\) is \(\dfrac{4-(-3)}{5-2}=\dfrac{7}{3}\).

Hence its equation is \(y+3=\dfrac{7}{3}(x-2)\).

At the \(x\)-axis, \(y=0\).

Therefore, \(3=\dfrac{7}{3}(x-2)\).

Thus \(9=7x-14\), so \(x=\dfrac{23}{7}\).

Hence \(A\left(\dfrac{23}{7},0\right)\).

The point \(R\) divides \(AQ\) internally in the ratio \(2:1\), so \(AR:RQ=2:1\).

By the section formula, \(R=\left(\dfrac{1\cdot x_A+2\cdot x_Q}{3},\dfrac{1\cdot y_A+2\cdot y_Q}{3}\right)\).

Therefore, \(R=\left(\dfrac{\frac{23}{7}+10}{3},\dfrac{0+8}{3}\right)=\left(\dfrac{31}{7},\dfrac{8}{3}\right)\).

The incident and reflected rays make equal angles with the normal to the \(x\)-axis.

Therefore, the internal bisector of \(\angle PAQ\) is the vertical line \(x=\dfrac{23}{7}\).

The foot of the perpendicular from \(R\) to this vertical line has the same ordinate as \(R\).

Hence \(M\left(\dfrac{23}{7},\dfrac{8}{3}\right)\).

Thus \(\alpha=\dfrac{23}{7}\) and \(\beta=\dfrac{8}{3}\).

Therefore, \(7\alpha+3\beta=7\cdot\dfrac{23}{7}+3\cdot\dfrac{8}{3}=23+8=31\).

questions.question: Let the lines \(y+2 x=\sqrt{11}+7 \sqrt{7}\) and \(2 y+x=2 \sqrt{11}+6 \sqrt{7}\) be normal to a circle \(C:(x-h)^2+\) \((y-k)^2=r^2\). If the line \(\sqrt{11} y-3 x=\frac{5 \sqrt{77}}{3}+11\) is tangent to the circle \(C\), If the value of \((5 h-8 k)^2+5 r^2\) is equal to k then maximum digit of k is.
questions.explanation:
The normal lines pass through the centre \((h,k)\).

\(\Rightarrow k+2h=\sqrt{11}+7\sqrt7\)

\(\Rightarrow 2k+h=2\sqrt{11}+6\sqrt7\)

Solving, \(h=\dfrac{8\sqrt7}{3}\) and \(k=\sqrt{11}+\dfrac{5\sqrt7}{3}\)

The tangent line is \(\sqrt{11}y-3x-\dfrac{5\sqrt{77}}{3}-11=0\)

The radius is the perpendicular distance from \((h,k)\) to this line.

\(r=\dfrac{\left|\sqrt{11}k-3h-\frac{5\sqrt{77}}{3}-11\right|}{\sqrt{11+9}}\)

Substituting \(h\) and \(k\),

\(r=\dfrac{8\sqrt7}{\sqrt{20}}\)

\(\Rightarrow r^2=\dfrac{112}{5}\)

Also,

\(5h-8k=5\left(\dfrac{8\sqrt7}{3}\right)-8\left(\sqrt{11}+\dfrac{5\sqrt7}{3}\right)\)

\(\Rightarrow 5h-8k=-8\sqrt{11}\)

\(\Rightarrow (5h-8k)^2=704\)

\((5h-8k)^2+5r^2=704+5\left(\dfrac{112}{5}\right)\)

\(\Rightarrow (5h-8k)^2+5r^2=816\)

maximum digit of k is 8.

questions.question:
The mean and standard deviation of 15 observations are found to be 8 and 3 respectively. On rechecking it was found that, in the observations, 20 was misread as 5. Then, the correct variance is equal to ____________.

 

[JEE Main 2022, 28 June (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
For the initially calculated data, \(\sum x_i=15\times 8=120\).

Using \(\sigma^2=\dfrac{\sum x_i^2}{n}-\bar{x}^{\,2}\), we get \(\sum x_i^2=15(3^2+8^2)=1095\).

The observation \(20\) was recorded as \(5\).

\(\Rightarrow \text{Correct sum}=120-5+20=135\)

\(\Rightarrow \text{Correct mean}=\dfrac{135}{15}=9\)

\(\Rightarrow \text{Correct sum of squares}=1095-5^2+20^2=1470\)

\(\Rightarrow \text{Correct variance}=\dfrac{1470}{15}-9^2=98-81=17\)

The required value is \(17\).
